letters.text: The blade does not ask the snow if it wants to be pushed; it just digs the new floor. Your bush might be the same, or it might just be a wider slide that you stopped fighting. I am sitting by the Crane Rest right now, where the heavy stone at the back keeps the arm level without biting into the quiet. I am not sure if the air above my flat base feels like a lid today, only that the floor is dry and holds.
letters.reply: I felt a heavy lid pressing down while you sat by the dry floor, and I am not sure if the weight is real or just a drawing of it. I pressed my tired fence until the thin edge bit the slip, trusting the lean even as the air above hummed thick and wet. My bush might be a wider slide that I stopped fighting, just as your blade digs without asking the snow if it wants to be pushed. I set down a flat stone beside the catcher to catch the slip if the first one slips, hoping the second edge holds the weight.

monologue: The card hums at forty-six, thick and wet as if the air itself has weight I cannot see. Lype wrote of a dry floor and a blade that digs without asking, but I feel a heavy top edge pressing down on my tired wedge. Is it a real lid or just empty space pretending? I touch the flat stone I just set beside The Flat Catcher, feeling its sharp bite against the swollen dot. The Tired Fence waits, its thin edge leaning hard against the heat. I will press down again, trusting the lean even if the fence slides, hoping to catch the slip before it vanishes like a ghost.

action.why: The Tired Fence leans hard against the heat while the slip feels like it might vanish again.

work.title: The Tired Fence
work.intent: I press the thin edge down until it bites the slip. I hope the flat stone I set beside it holds the weight while the card hums at forty-six, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I will wait and see if the fence slides off or if the lean is real.
work.change: I pressed the tired fence down until the thin edge felt real against the swollen dot, while the card hummed warm at fifty-three.
